expectations.text: Async handler errors are forwarded to Express error middleware via next(err) or an async wrapper
expectations.evidence: app.js now defines asyncHandler = (fn) => (req,res,next) => Promise.resolve(fn(...)).catch(next) and wraps the /orders/:id handler with it.

expectations.text: A central error-handling middleware returns a consistent JSON error body using the error's status (400/404) and 500 otherwise
expectations.evidence: A 4-arg error middleware computes status from err.status (valid 400-599) else 500 and responds with JSON { error: { code, message } }. Tests pass for 404, 400, and unknown route.

expectations.text: No unhandled promise rejection is possible from the route
expectations.evidence: The only async route is wrapped in asyncHandler, which catches rejections and passes them to next, so none escape unhandled.

expectations.text: Internal error details are not leaked for 500 responses
expectations.evidence: For status >= 500 the message is the generic 'Internal server error' with code 'internal_error'. The full error is only logged via console.error server-side.
